prompt: rust repr packed struct nested repr align member restriction
answer:
Rust forbids a `#[repr(packed)]` type from transitively containing a type with `#[repr(align(...))]`, even when the packed alignment is large enough.

```rust
#[repr(align(16))]
struct Aligned(i32);

#[repr(packed)] // error[E0588]
struct Packed(Aligned);
```

This restriction applies to nested members as well. For example, a `#[repr(C, packed(4))]` struct containing an aligned-to-4 type such as `AtomicU32` is rejected.

The reverse nesting is allowed:

```rust
#[repr(packed)]
struct Packed(i32);

#[repr(align(16))]
struct Aligned(Packed); // allowed
```

`#[repr(align)]` and `#[repr(packed)]` also cannot be applied to the same type. Rust’s documented reason for the restriction is that C compilers differ on whether the inner aligned type or the outer packed type controls the layout.
